chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn 'Amr from Ibn Sinan from Abi al-Jarud from Sa'd al-Iskafi from al-Asbagh from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said:
Any ruler who hides himself from the needs of the people, Allah will hide from him on the Day of Resurrection and from his own needs.
And if he accepts a gift, it is considered betrayal of trust (ghulul).
And if he takes a bribe, he is a polytheist.

key_terms.غُلُولًا: Betrayal of trust / spoils of war taken treacherously

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences for a ruler who neglects the people's needs or takes bribes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS) in *Thawab al-A'mal* underscores the concept of *al-Imamah* as a divine trust, where a ruler's accessibility (*kashr al-hijab*) is directly linked to divine accessibility. Shaykh al-Saduq uses this to highlight that accepting gifts (*hadiyyah*) constitutes *ghulul* (plunder/betrayal of trust), while bribes (*rishwah*) elevate to *shirk* due to the distortion of justice, a key theme in Shia political ethics.
